_comment: Golden dev set for the BUNDLED SAMPLE CORPUS (data/samples/, fictional founders). Use it to run the evaluation harness end-to-end on a fresh clone, before any real media has been swept: EVAL_GOLDENS_FILE=goldens.samples.json python scripts/evaluate.py --retrieval. Every `evidence` string is a verbatim span of the shipped sample text, so labels are checkable by grep. The default set, goldens.json, is labelled against a real swept corpus and will report broken labels until you have collected that media.

_negative_controls_comment: Questions the sample corpus CANNOT answer. They carry no evidence by design, so they are kept out of `goldens` (where an evidence-less entry is reported as a broken label) and scored separately by evaluate_abstention(). Without these the harness cannot see the pipeline's most dangerous failure: answering confidently, with citations, when nothing retrieved supports an answer. n13 is deliberately adversarial - it shares common tokens ('2019', 'won') with a passage about a default-rate crisis, which defeated a content-word heuristic on its own.
